_comment_overview: Three things here: (1) `hooks.PreToolUse` runs block_dangerous_commands.py on every Bash/PowerShell call — blocks rm -rf, git push --force, git reset --hard, reading .env, printing $TOKEN, etc. (2) `hooks.PostToolUse` runs verify_comments_only.py after every Write/Edit — if the file is under backend/app, backend/tests, backend/alembic or frontend/src it compares the Python AST (and TS code lines) against git HEAD and warns if code changed, not just comments. Silent when clean; only speaks up on a real difference. Added because annotating files means rewriting them, and a dropped or duplicated line has twice slipped past the test suite. (3) `permissions.allow` pre-approves the read-mostly + test + build + git-local commands used most often on this project, so the assistant doesn't need to re-ask for them every turn. Anything not listed still prompts you the first time. Adapted from claude-code-bmad-foundation.
